ei.title: A Brief History of Ellis Island (복습)
ei.subject: Ellis Island (양지원 학교 유인물)

fullPassage: In the late 1800s, people in many parts of the world decided to leave their homes for reasons such as crop failure, land and job shortages, rising taxes, famine, and relief from political and religious persecution. Perceiving the United States as the land of opportunity, nearly 12 million immigrants immigrated to the United States between 1870 and 1900. Together, these immigrants shaped a big part of the work force that drove the industrialization of America and helped the United States emerge as an industrial powerhouse. During this time, more than 70 percent of all immigrants entered through New York City, which came to be known as the “Golden Door.” Around 1892 when Ellis Island opened as a new immigration processing center, Americans became concerned with the “quality” of immigrants arriving in the country. The 1891 Immigration Act had set the course of American immigration policy for the next thirty years by expanding the types of “undesirable” immigrants. In addition to physical problems such as poor eyesight, bad backs, and trachoma, Ellis Island officials were on the lookout for “idiots, insane persons, paupers or persons likely to become public charges, persons suffering from a loathsome or a dangerous disease, persons who have been convicted of a crime or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude, polygamists.” In the coming decades, the list kept growing. In the 1920s, various immigration quota acts restricted immigration in numbers. The role Ellis Island held gradually shifted to that of a detention center for suspected Nazi and fascist sympathizers, and later, for suspected Communists and other radicals awaiting deportation. By 1954, an increasingly irrelevant Ellis Island closed its doors. Today, Ellis Island has transformed into a popular tourist attraction, after processing at least one ancestor of some 40 percent of Americans, according to estimations. As America deals with the challenges of our latest wave of mass immigration, it will do so without Ellis Island. But Ellis Island as myth, as a memory place, still has an important hold on the American imagination, and future generations will grapple with both its historical meaning and its relevance to contemporary, multicultural America.

det.korean: ②have restricted → restricted. 'In the 1920s(1920년대에)'라는 명백한 과거 시점 표현이 있으므로 현재완료(have p.p.)가 아니라 단순 과거 restricted를 써야 해요.

빈칸 문장: 'Americans became ___ (concern) with the "quality" of immigrants'.

→ concern은 원래 '(누구를) 염려하게 하다'라는 동사예요. 사람이 주어라서 '염려하는' 상태를 나타내려면 과거분사 concerned로 바꿔요.
→ 'become + 감정 과거분사'는 '~한 기분이 되다'예요. 그래서 became concerned(염려하게 되었다)가 돼요.
→ 참고로 concerning(-ing형)은 '걱정을 일으키는(대상)'이라 사람 주어에는 안 맞아요.
